question: My screen went black for a few seconds at 9:42 while I was playing, then came back. What happened?

causes.rationale: Display event 4101 at 09:42:07 reports that amdkmdag stopped responding and recovered, and two seconds later Windows Error Reporting filed LiveKernelEvent 141 (VIDEO_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_DETECTED) against amdkmdag.sys. That is a TDR: the GPU missed the two-second watchdog, Windows reset it, and the display came back. The 2.1 s frame directly before the reset is the black screen the user saw.

GPU hotspot climbed from 71 °C to 106 °C over eight minutes of sustained load and fell to 74 °C once the GPU reset. It stayed under the 110 °C throttle point, so heat is a plausible contributor to the hang but is not shown to be the cause.
game.exe was the only heavy GPU client. A hang inside the game would freeze its own window but would not normally trigger a kernel-mode TDR with a live dump, so this is unlikely.

next_steps: Clean-install the current AMD Adrenalin driver (the installed amdkmdag is 32.0.21013.1000 from July) and retest the same game session.
Check case airflow and the GPU fan curve; retest once with the power limit lowered by 10% to see whether the timeouts stop.
If it happens again, attach the live kernel dump from C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports\WATCHDOG to an AMD bug report.

bug_report.title: amdkmdag TDR (LiveKernelEvent 141) during sustained 3D load on driver 32.0.21013.1000
bug_report.summary: While a game was running, the display went black for about two seconds and then recovered. The System log records Display event 4101 for amdkmdag, followed by a LiveKernelEvent 141 (VIDEO_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_DETECTED) report. GPU hotspot temperature was 106 °C just before the timeout.
steps_to_reproduce: Run a GPU-bound 3D game at 1440p, uncapped frame rate, for about ten minutes.
Watch for the display going black and recovering.
bug_report.expected: The game keeps rendering with stable frame times and the driver does not reset.
bug_report.actual: Frame time spiked to 2.1 s, the screen went black, and Windows reset the display driver (Display 4101, LiveKernelEvent 141).

evidence.label: amdkmdag 32.0.21013.1000 (2026-07-14)
evidence.detail: Display adapter driver: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc., oem42.inf, signed.

evidence.label: game.exe started
evidence.detail: Working set 6.1 GB; the only process with sustained GPU load.

evidence.label: GPU hotspot
evidence.detail: Junction temperature (LibreHardwareMonitor); edge 84 °C. Peak for the session.

evidence.label: GPU hotspot
evidence.detail: Junction temperature (LibreHardwareMonitor); edge 66 °C after the driver reset.

evidence.label: Frame time hitch
evidence.detail: PresentMon, game.exe; GPU busy for the whole interval, no frames presented.

evidence.label: Frame time hitch
evidence.detail: PresentMon, game.exe; last frame before the device was removed and reset.

evidence.label: Frame time
evidence.detail: PresentMon, game.exe; rendering resumed after recovery.

evidence.label: Display 4101: amdkmdag stopped responding and has recovered
evidence.detail: System log, provider Display, event 4101, record 48211: Display driver amdkmdag stopped responding and has successfully recovered.

evidence.label: LiveKernelEvent 141 (VIDEO_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_DETECTED)
evidence.detail: Application log, Windows Error Reporting event 1001, record 90377: LiveKernelEvent, P1 141, bucket LKD_0x141_Tdr:6_IMAGE_amdkmdag.sys_Navi32. Dump: C:\Windows\LiveKernelReports\WATCHDOG\WATCHDOG-20261020-0942.dmp.
